text:
[IRET.9.6] **Ill-typed operations and renderings split three ways, and `null`
is the first test.** Arithmetic on wrong types (e.g. adding a `String` to an
`Int`) yields **no value**, and so does a format spec the value it is given
cannot render (a numeric spec over a `Json` leaf holding a string). Both
raise, and which fault they raise depends on the operand:

- **An operand is `null` — `TypeError`.** A `null` in a slot declared `T?` is
  a value the artefact **declared**, so absence is data and is never evidence
  that the artefact lied. The activation is abandoned. This arm is reached
  only where an operation refuses a `null` at all, which is a narrow set: a
  conversion yields `null` for a null source rather than raising, and `null`
  propagates through arithmetic and comparison ([LNUL.4.1]). What
  remains is the builtins that demand a value of a particular kind — and a
  `T?` slot cannot reach one, because a builtin's receiver and its arguments
  are both concrete-value positions ([LNUL.5.1]) and an un-narrowed nullable
  is refused there at compile time. The route that remains is a `Json`
  projection whose leaf is a present JSON `null` ([LNUL.8.4]) — a value rather
  than absence, carried by a slot whose shape is not schema-committed, and so
  not refused before it runs. A narrowed `T?` ([LNUL.5.4]) meets this arm only
  when the conjunct it narrows is evaluated before its guard; the guard is then
  `false`, and absorbs the `TypeError` ([LNUL.4.2]).
- **Neither operand is `null`, and one derives from a `Json` slot —
  `TypeError`.** A wrong-typed `Json` value is data, whether it is a leaf a
  projection reached or the whole slot read directly. `Json` is the one slot
  type whose shape is not schema-committed ([LADP.5.5.3]), so this is expected
  in normal operation and attributable to a node. The activation is abandoned.
- **Otherwise — `EngineError`.** The load-time shape said one thing and the
  value is another, so the artefact lied and nothing about it is trustworthy.
  The tier halts.

**Each disposition is that of a fault the expression yields.** A deciding
operand of `and` / `or` absorbs any of the three ([LNUL.4.2]): an absorbed
`TypeError` abandons nothing, an absorbed `EngineError` does not halt the tier,
and neither reaches a surface ([LERR.1.4.11]). An `EngineError` the expression
yields halts the tier, and that run is outside the determinism guarantee
([LDET.1.11]).

**The order of the first two tests is normative, not an implementation
detail.** A `null` reaching an operation through a `Json` projection is both
null and tainted, and both orderings classify it `TypeError`. The rule is that
**absence decides before provenance**, because absence is data whatever
carried it, and provenance is only the question of whether a *present* value's
type can be trusted.

Provenance starts at **every read of a `Json` slot**, a bare slot read as well
as a projection. Provenance is **transitive** — `(j.a + 1) > 5` buries the
projection a level down — and a raising site sees only a tag and a union. So provenance is computed
by the compiler and lowered onto the node as `Expr.json_tainted`
(`proto/rete_expr.proto`); the evaluator reads it, it does not derive it.

Taint **flows** through a `let` and **clears** at a `::` cast and at `??`: both
establish the type and carry their own disposition, so a later ill-typed
operation on the far side means something else is wrong — the `EngineError`
criterion exactly. Taint is **rule-local**; a value reaching a slot has passed
through `emit` into a schema-committed slot, so provenance ends at the fact
boundary.

An absent flag means clean: proto3 has no presence for a scalar.

**An interpolation segment carries the flag like any other node.** A segment
reading a `Json` value is tainted, so a format spec that cannot render it
abandons the activation rather than halting the tier — the same disposition
the same value gets one operator away ([LADP.5.5.3]). A null or absent value
is not this case: it renders as the empty string ([LGRA.2.9.6.2]) and raises
nothing.

⚠ **`Json` path traversal is NOT one of these.** [LNUL.8.4] governs it: an
unresolved path reads as `null`, and a path resolving to a JSON `null` reads as
`null` **as a present value**. Both are `null`; `has(path)` is what tells them
apart, and it is the only absence test. An unresolved path is absence, not an
ill-typed operation, and it does not abandon the activation.

alloy.name: iret_9_6__honest
alloy.note: The artefact did not lie: no conjunct yields an EngineError, the third arm of [IRET.9.6]. The determinism guarantee is scoped to such runs ([LDET.1.11]).

alloy.name: iret_9_6__v5_lie_breaks_hoisting
alloy.note: WHY THE ARTEFACT MUST NOT LIE: a hoisted conjunct over a value the artefact lied about raises its EngineError alone and blocks the `no` pattern, where the whole `where` is false.

idris.name: lstr_2_1__len_is_total_on_texts
idris.note: The first arm at a builtin's receiver: `len` of a `null` String is a trap, the TypeError that abandons the activation, and of every text an Int. Partial because the clause says an un-narrowed `String?` cannot reach a builtin's receiver ([LNUL.5.1]); the model answers for the form all the same, and a guard `is not null` before the `len` absorbs the trap ([LNUL.4.2]), as Main.idr runs.

idris.name: lstr_2_1__len_of
idris.note: `len(<String>)` of `null`: the first arm, a TypeError, a trap here. Partial because the clause says the route is refused at compile time for an un-narrowed `String?` and is reached through a `Json` leaf alone; the model has no Json `len` of a String leaf (`lexp_6_1__len` counts an array) and answers for the slot form.

idris.name: rlow_5_5__faulting_filter_differs
idris.note: WHY NO FAULT: a filter raising an EngineError -- an artefact that lied, [IRET.9.6] -- raises it alone and blocks a `no` pattern where the `where` is false. So two engines may differ on an artefact that lies, which is why [LDET.1.11] scopes the guarantee to one that does not.
